prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (alias/call sign: Juniper) is the region’s primary dispatch and coordination point, providing continuous intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, and coordination under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols. It maintains a shared operational picture of incidents, units, and access constraints. Participating jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local policy responsibility; the regional service coordinates agreed response activity.
Call Taker Mara confirms incident location/details and enters requests via the Computer Aided Dispatch Console. Triage Supervisor reviews and assigns/confirms priority; Regional Medical Director establishes clinical triage policies and protocol limits. Dispatch personnel apply approved protocols and seek guidance beyond delegated authority. Shift Commander (alias/call sign: Sundial) manages operational coordination, continuity, conflicts, surge priorities, and escalation, without superseding clinical-policy authority or Paramedic Crew scene-level judgment. Paramedic Crew assesses and treats within scope and protocols.
Radio Coordinator (alias/call sign: Mistral) monitors the Regional Radio Network, maintains clear communications, confirms channel availability and backup-procedure understanding at shift start; radio checks test weak-signal coverage and identify problems. Radio Coordinator supports communications among dispatch personnel and ambulance crews. Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias/call sign: Bluejay) monitors vehicle availability, servicing, defects, and coverage constraints; produces Battery Swap Voucher documenting authorized battery replacement. Readiness checks confirm staffing, communications equipment, clinical supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, and maintenance restrictions for available ambulances. Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, and information-handling compliance.
Operating area is divided into defined response zones reflecting distance, road access, and ambulance capacity. Zone boundaries are maintained with jurisdictions and reviewed when roads, population, or agreements change. Each zone has primary/alternate routes to the Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center, subject to clinical direction and access. Dispatch considers travel time, restrictions, weather, and closures; crews verify rapidly changing conditions before constrained routes. North Gate Status Board presents northern access/queue conditions and produces North Approach Queue Snapshot. South Gate Status Board presents southern access conditions, including ambulance-entry restrictions. Both boards are checked at shift start and when reported changes may affect response or hospital arrival. Ambulance Coordination Platform supports incident, assignment, and resource-status views; Ambulance Unit 417 is in the regional pool when assigned. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates receiving-capacity/destination awareness; Emergency Department communicates receiving considerations. Riverside Trauma Center is assessed for availability/suitability. Regional Radio Network carries authorized responder communications.

New part:
S044: The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
S045: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
S046: The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
S047: The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
S048: The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
S049: The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
S050: Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
S051: The Regional Dispatch Center handles incoming emergency calls through a controlled intake process that creates an incident record for coordination.
S052: Call Taker Mara is also known by the radio alias Larkspur.
S053: The Hospital Liaison Desk is also known by the coordination alias Kestrel.
S054: Call Taker Mara establishes the caller's location before collecting medical details.
S055: Call Taker Mara asks for the street address, municipality, and any building, floor, or entrance information needed to find the patient.
S056: Call Taker Mara confirms the location by repeating the address and checking it against the caller's description of nearby landmarks.
S057: Call Taker Mara asks whether the caller can provide a callback number in case the connection is lost.
S058: Call Taker Mara gathers the patient's age, level of consciousness, breathing status, and the main reason emergency help is needed.
S059: Call Taker Mara uses direct questions to distinguish observed symptoms from information reported by someone else.
S060: Call Taker Mara records the time symptoms began when the caller can provide a reliable estimate.
S061: Call Taker Mara notes access barriers such as locked entrances, restricted roads, or difficulty reaching the patient.
S062: Call Taker Mara produces the Caller Location Correction Slip when the caller's address needs documented clarification.
S063: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks entered location details against available address and map data.
S064: If the location does not resolve cleanly, Call Taker Mara asks focused follow-up questions and updates the incident record.
S065: Call Taker Mara remains engaged with the caller when further information could change the response priority or access plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
